name: D-Day
summary: 6 June 1944 landings on Utah, Omaha, Gold, Juno, and Sword. Overview jump, not a single unit pin.
source: Published Normandy landing beaches. Confirm against SHAEF / army group situation maps.

name: Brécourt Manor
summary: 6 June, Brécourt Manor. Featured Easy Company pin.
source: Published Brécourt Manor site 49.390056, -1.226111. Confirm against 506th PIR S-3 / AAR.

name: Gold
summary: 6 June, Gold sector Jig (Asnelles / Le Hamel). Featured Sherwood Rangers landing.
source: Published location of Le Hamel / Gold Jig. Confirm against TNA WO 171 SRY and 50th Division diaries.

name: Carentan
summary: Carentan, 10–12 June. Easy Company and 101st / 506th pins use this town.
source: Published commune location, Carentan. Confirm against 101st G-3 and 506th PIR S-3 / AAR.

name: Tulle
summary: 9 June, Tulle. 2nd SS Das Reich on the march north. Off the Normandy camera frame.
source: Published commune location, Tulle. Confirm against Das Reich KTB.

name: Oradour
summary: 10 June, Oradour-sur-Glane. I./Der Führer only. Do not stack Tulle, Oradour, and Mortain on one marker.
source: Published location of Oradour-sur-Glane. Confirm against I./Der Führer records.

name: Villers-Bocage
summary: 13 June, Villers-Bocage. Tagged to 4th County of London Yeomanry and s.SS-Pz.Abt. 101. Not the Sherwood Rangers.
source: Published commune location, Villers-Bocage. Confirm against TNA WO 171 4 CLY and s.SS-Pz.Abt. 101 records.

name: Point 103
summary: 9–13 June, Point 103 / Saint-Pierre. Sherwood Rangers Yeomanry. Laycock is killed here on 11 June.
source: Published location of Point 103 near Saint-Pierre, Calvados. Confirm against TNA WO 171 SRY and 8th Armoured Brigade diaries.

name: Arromanches
summary: 6 June, Arromanches-les-Bains. 1st Battalion, Hampshire Regiment, on the western Gold flank. Later Mulberry B.
source: Published commune location, Arromanches-les-Bains. Wikipedia Operation Overlord (Wilmot). Confirm against TNA WO 171 1st Hampshire / 50th Division diaries.

name: Cherbourg
summary: 26 June, Cherbourg captured. 9th, 4th, and 79th Infantry Divisions after fighting from 19 June. Port wrecked; not fully working until September. No pin for the 17 June west-coast cut-off; that town is unnamed in Overlord.
source: Published commune location, Cherbourg-en-Cotentin. Wikipedia Operation Overlord (Ford & Zaloga). Confirm against VII Corps G-3.

name: Caen (Charnwood)
summary: 8–9 July, Operation Charnwood. Northern Caen occupied north of the Orne after bombing on the evening of 7 July. Overlord does not name the Allied divisions on this day.
source: Published commune location, Caen. Wikipedia Operation Overlord (Copp; Beevor). Confirm against I Corps and 3rd Division war diaries.

name: Caen (Goodwood)
summary: 18–21 July, Operations Atlantic and Goodwood. Rest of Caen and the high ground to the south. City nearly destroyed. Overlord does not name the Allied divisions on this day.
source: Published commune location, Caen. Wikipedia Operation Overlord (Ford & Zaloga). Confirm against VIII Corps and II Canadian Corps war diaries.

name: Saint-Lô
summary: 25 July, Operation Cobra. U.S. First Army launches the breakout after securing the Cotentin south as far as Saint-Lô. Overlord does not name a division in the town that day.
source: Published commune location, Saint-Lô. Wikipedia Operation Overlord (Beevor). Confirm against First Army G-3.

name: Vire
summary: 30 July, Operation Bluecoat begins, aiming to secure Vire and Mont Pinçon. This pin is the named objective, not a sourced capture that day.
source: Published commune location, Vire. Wikipedia Operation Overlord (Beevor). Confirm against VIII Corps war diaries.

name: Avranches
summary: 1 August, U.S. First Army at Avranches after Cobra. Third Army activates the same day. Overlord does not name a division in the town.
source: Published commune location, Avranches. Wikipedia Operation Overlord (Beevor). Confirm against First Army G-3.

name: Alençon
summary: 11 August, U.S. Third Army reaches Alençon on the southern hook of the Falaise encirclement. Overlord does not name a division in the town.
source: Published commune location, Alençon. Wikipedia Operation Overlord (Beevor). Confirm against Third Army G-3.

name: Falaise
summary: 16 August, Canadians capture Falaise. The gap closes on 21 August. Tagged to 3rd Canadian Division already in this pack; Overlord names the Canadians, not a single division. 2nd Canadian Division is not pinned.
source: Published commune location, Falaise. Wikipedia Operation Overlord (Wilmot). Confirm against First Canadian Army and 3rd Canadian Division war diaries.

name: Paris
summary: 25 August, Paris liberated. French 2e DB arrived from the west on 24 August; U.S. 4th Infantry Division pressed from the south.
source: Published commune location, Paris. Wikipedia Operation Overlord (Wilmot). Confirm against 2e DB and 4th Infantry Division records.

name: Elbeuf
summary: 25 August, U.S. 2nd Armored Division fights into Elbeuf and meets British and Canadian armour.
source: Published commune location, Elbeuf. Wikipedia Operation Overlord (Stacey). Confirm against 2nd Armored Division G-3.

name: Rouen
summary: 30 August, 3rd Canadian Infantry Division crosses the Seine near Elbeuf and enters Rouen.
source: Published commune location, Rouen. Wikipedia Operation Overlord (Stacey). Confirm against 3rd Canadian Division war diary.
